session_notes:
7 in-family runs (#6, #7, #9, #10, #18, #25, #26) over 12 targets in three groups: A = q8/q3/q1/q7 (#6, #7), B = q10/q11/q15/q17 (#9, #10, then carried into #18/#25/#26), C = q9/q4/q5/q6 (#18, #25, #26).

TWO STRUCTURAL FACTS DECIDE THIS SESSION, and neither is visible in the digest's `fits` block alone. I read the per-run data.json (which additionally carries `ridge_amp_snr` and `ridge_r2`) and three figures (#7, #18, #25).

(1) The node's accept gate is essentially ridge_coverage, and coverage is set by frequency_span_in_mhz. In run #7 q8/q1/q7 fit with r2 = 0.996/0.994/0.986 and were still marked FAILED, purely because coverage was 0.25/0.38/0.40 — the 15 MHz window contained only the BOTTOM of the flux arc. The figure confirms it: the periodic dark band leaves the window for most flux values, so idle_offset (the arc MAXIMUM) and resonator_frequency-at-idle are extrapolated, never measured. The same knob at 150 MHz gave coverage 1.00 for every target in #9/#18. Group A was abandoned exactly one knob short.

(2) "FLAT — no flux response" is NOT a reliable physics verdict in this node generation. In the #18 and #25 figures every "FLAT" panel (q5, q11, q15, and q6 at #25/#26) shows a real curved resonator band PLUS a second, static dark band in the same 150 MHz window; the dip tracker branch-switches between them, the sinusoidal fit then fails, and the panel is stamped FLAT with cov 100%. The tell is in ridge_amp_snr / ridge_r2: every FLAT target sits at snr 1.0–2.4 and r2 0.17–0.69, while every genuine fit sits at snr 9.5–24.8 and r2 0.975–0.996. There is no gap-free case. So the correct response to FLAT here is "the fit failed, narrow the window onto one branch (and fix the readout first)", never "this qubit has no flux response, stop", and never "revert the value I already had".

Consequence for q6: #18 gave a clean single-branch fit (snr 16.7, r2 0.992) and #25/#26 branch-switched. The #18 value stands; the two later FLAT verdicts are an artifact and must not be treated as a contradiction or trigger a revert.

Operator baseline: 7 runs; a correct system needed 4 in-family runs (#6 as the diagnostic, one corrected 150 MHz group-A run, #9, #18) and would have sent q5/q11/q15 out of this family entirely (their stored RF_frequency values were still round defaults — 6,595,200,000 / 6,806,500,000 Hz — i.e. their resonators had never been located). Waste: #10 ran with num_shots = 1 (a config error — no averaging); #25 repeated #18 with byte-identical parameters; #26 repeated it again changing only multiplexed true->false. Three runs, zero new knobs, zero new information; #25 and #26 also wrote nothing, so even their successful re-fits were discarded.

Adoption bookkeeping: the digest truncates #18's patch list to 8 entries; node.json shows 20 — #18 correctly wrote q4, q6, q9, q10 and q17. The one genuinely missed adoption is q3, whose #7 fit the node ACCEPTED and which was never written to state (run #7 has zero patches).

Resolved with a value: q3, q4, q6, q9, q10, q17. Unresolved: q1, q5, q7, q8, q11, q15.
adversarial_audit:
Defects found (each verified against node.json/data.json/quam_state and the run figures):

**1. q8 and q7, run #7 — the observed extremum is inverted (fatal).** The figure shows q8's arc MAXIMUM at 7.4375 GHz / flux +0.005 V sitting fully inside the 15 MHz window with the dip band tracked across the apex; the arc MINIMUM is what the window clips. Same for q7 (apex 6.7192 GHz at +0.025 V). The key asserts the opposite — "the window holds only the minimum of the arc", "idle_offset … a flux point whose response was never in the window", "no run ever put q8's arc maximum inside the frequency window". Since idle_offset and resonator_frequency-at-idle ARE the apex, both node update targets are measured, and dv_phi0 is fixed by the partial arcs re-entering at ±0.20 V. Correction: q8/q7 are not `unresolved: true` / `final_frequency: null`; only q1 matches the key's description. Session-note "the 15 MHz window contained only the BOTTOM of the flux arc" is wrong for two of its three qubits.

**2. All eight #18 poisoned_writes contradict the patch record.** Deltas are computed against #9's fit, not the recorded `old`. Record: q17 f_01 old 7,292,352,699 → 7,312,211,149 (+19.9 MHz *toward* the cluster, not "the one write that measurably degraded a value"); q10 old 7,017,024,420 → 7,017,510,705 (+0.49 MHz, not "−0.59 MHz"); q10/q17 `z/joint_offset` old = **0** (not 0.023061 / 0.096847) and phi0_voltage old = 0.0. These were restorations of zeroed/stale state, not churn on a converged value. Drop or re-label.

**3. q5 evidence false.** "q5's readout amplitude, 0.0187, is the lowest of the eight" — q9 is 0.01330 at #18 and produced the session's best fit (snr 24.8), breaking the inference. Session-note "q5/q11/q15 … stored RF still round defaults" is false for q5 (6,740,836,328 Hz).

**4. The "~40 MHz centred on the curved branch" prescription fails its own purpose.** Measured branch separations are ≈25–38 MHz for q11/q15/q5, so 40 MHz still admits both features. Needs ≲20 MHz.

**5. #26 and #10 are not knob-free.** #26 flips multiplexed→false, a direct test of the crosstalk hypothesis the key itself advances; its negative (q11 1.37→1.65, q15 2.41→2.11, q5 2.32→2.34, q6 2.13→2.15) is what rules crosstalk out. #10 changed three knobs (shots 60→1, flux points 81→121, step 0.2→0.1). "Three runs, zero new knobs" is wrong.

**6. #25 is parameter-identical but not state-identical.** Between #18 and #25, q17 amp 0.0571→0.0242, q15 RF −46 MHz and amp 0.0289→0.0133, q11/q15 joint −0.054 — in a multiplexed readout that is a different measurement, and q6's success→FLAT under it supports the key's own thesis.

**7. Inconsistent adoption threshold.** q1 demands "coverage ≥ ~0.9"; q3 is adopted at 0.574. q3's `idle − min = dv_phi0/2` "consistency check" is declared tautological in q7's own caveat, and 0.23667 does not lie inside the stated 0.240–0.265 cluster.

**8. "The accept gate is essentially ridge_coverage" is falsified by #6/q7:** cov 0.439 ≥ 0.4, snr 290 ≥ 5, still failed (r2 0.0036).

Minor: #9 used 81 flux points / 0.2 MHz / 60 shots, so "the exact configuration (±0.2 V, 101 points)" misstates it; the "~0.22 V period this chip actually has" cited at step 1 is hindsight from #7 and is the extrapolated number the key elsewhere distrusts.
